POST /v1/batch/info.batch_id: Batch id from the submit response.
POST /v1/batch/info.limit: How many items to return in items (pagination).

POST /v1/claim/{token}.address: Recipient address in the payout network.
POST /v1/claim/{token}.memo: Memo/tag — only for networks where it is required.
POST /v1/claim/{token}.passcode: Claim code — if the sender set one on the link. After 10 incorrect attempts the link is locked.

POST /v1/documents/jobs.format: File format: pdf (default) or csv. CSV is generated without layout — cheaper for large statements and loads into Excel/1C.
POST /v1/documents/jobs.from: Start of the period, YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to the first day of the current month).
POST /v1/documents/jobs.kind: Report type: statement (operations), fees (commissions) or ledger (balance movements).
POST /v1/documents/jobs.to: End of the period, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to today). The period may span up to two years.

POST /v1/documents/jobs/info.job_id: Job id from the creation response.

POST /v1/exchange-rate/list.currency_from: Currency code. If set, only its rate is returned. If empty or the body is {}, rates for all currencies are returned.
POST /v1/exchange-rate/list.currency_to: Quote currency: USDT by default; any pricing asset, including fiats with a direct feed (EUR, RUB, …).
POST /v1/exchange-rate/list.offset: Offset from the start of the list; default 0.

POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.amount: Amount entered by the buyer, in the link's price currency; required for open and range, ignored for fixed.
POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.currency: Settlement currency — the coin the buyer pays with; needed only if the link did not pin pinned_currency.
POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.network: Settlement network; needed only if the link did not pin pinned_network.
POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.order_id: Shop order number from the embedded widget (data-oblodai-order-id); carried over to the invoice and to the webhook for matching with the order; not an idempotency key.
POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.payer_email: Buyer email — the cheque is sent there automatically after payment.

POST /v1/payment.accuracy_payment_percent: Under/overpayment tolerance, 0–5 %. Overrides the merchant setting.
POST /v1/payment.additional_data: Private merchant data, echoed back in webhooks (not visible to the buyer).
POST /v1/payment.currency: Price currency code: any of the 23 fiats (USD, EUR, RUB, …) or any coin (USDT, BTC, …). JPY and KRW have zero decimal places.
POST /v1/payment.is_payment_multiple: Allow paying up the remaining amount.
POST /v1/payment.is_refresh: Revive an expired invoice by order_id instead of creating a new one.
POST /v1/payment.lifetime_seconds: Invoice lifetime in seconds, 300–43200; default 3600. Values outside the range are clamped to the nearest bound.
POST /v1/payment.network: Settlement network (e.g. tron, ethereum). Optional — see the currency and network selection modes.
POST /v1/payment.order_id: Merchant reference; idempotency key. Strongly recommended.
POST /v1/payment.payer_email: Payer email. If set, a cheque is sent there automatically after payment; it is also the default recipient for POST /v1/payment/send-email.
POST /v1/payment.subtract: Deprecated: % of the network markup charged to the payer (0–100); payer-facing markups are configured via discount.
POST /v1/payment.to_currency: Settlement currency — the crypto used for payment. Defaults to currency (only if currency is a coin); with a fiat price set it explicitly or omit it together with network.
POST /v1/payment.url_callback: Per-invoice webhook. Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): delivery is signed with its secret.
POST /v1/payment.url_return: "Back to shop" link on the payment page.

POST /v1/payment/accuracy/set.accuracy_percent: Tolerance in percent, 1–5. Required when enabled: true; ignored when enabled: false (reset to 0). Capped at 5 %.

POST /v1/payment/autorefund/set.underpay: Refund the funds on an expired underpayment (wrong_amount).

POST /v1/payment/batch.on_error: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — halt processing after the first error.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments: Array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as POST /v1/payment; set order_id on every item: results are matched by it and it protects against duplicates.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.accuracy_payment_percent: Under/overpayment tolerance, 0–5 %. Overrides the merchant setting.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.additional_data: Private merchant data, echoed back in webhooks (not visible to the buyer).
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.currency: Price currency code: any of the 23 fiats (USD, EUR, RUB, …) or any coin (USDT, BTC, …). JPY and KRW have zero decimal places.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.is_payment_multiple: Allow paying up the remaining amount.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.is_refresh: Revive an expired invoice by order_id instead of creating a new one.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.lifetime_seconds: Invoice lifetime in seconds, 300–43200; default 3600. Values outside the range are clamped to the nearest bound.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.network: Settlement network (e.g. tron, ethereum). Optional — see the currency and network selection modes.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.order_id: Merchant reference; idempotency key. Strongly recommended.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.payer_email: Payer email. If set, a cheque is sent there automatically after payment; it is also the default recipient for POST /v1/payment/send-email.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.subtract: Deprecated: % of the network markup charged to the payer (0–100); payer-facing markups are configured via discount.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.to_currency: Settlement currency — the crypto used for payment. Defaults to currency (only if currency is a coin); with a fiat price set it explicitly or omit it together with network.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.url_callback: Per-invoice webhook. Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): delivery is signed with its secret.
POST /v1/payment/batch.payments.url_return: "Back to shop" link on the payment page.

POST /v1/payment/cancel.uuid: Invoice id in Oblodai. Either uuid or order_id is required; uuid takes priority.

POST /v1/payment/discount/set.currency: Currency. Empty = global default for all coins.
POST /v1/payment/discount/set.discount_percent: Percentage, from -99 to 99. Positive is a discount, negative is a markup.
POST /v1/payment/discount/set.network: Network. Empty = any network of this currency.

POST /v1/payment/fee-config/set.payer_pays_percent: Share of OUR commission paid by the buyer: 0 — the merchant pays (current behaviour), 100 — the buyer pays and the invoice is issued with a markup. Applies to invoices created AFTER the change.

POST /v1/payment/info.uuid: Invoice id in Oblodai. Either uuid or order_id is required; uuid takes priority.

POST /v1/payment/link.amount_fixed: Amount — for fixed mode; required in this mode.
POST /v1/payment/link.currency: Price currency — fiat (USD, EUR, RUB, …) or a coin; see pricing_currencies from GET /v1/currencies.
POST /v1/payment/link.expires_in_seconds: Link lifetime in seconds from creation; 0 (default) — the link never expires.
POST /v1/payment/link.max_amount: Upper bound — for range; required in this mode.
POST /v1/payment/link.min_amount: Lower bound: an optional floor for open, a required minimum for range.
POST /v1/payment/link.pinned_currency: Settlement currency (coin) pinned to the link; empty — the buyer chooses the coin.
POST /v1/payment/link.pinned_network: Settlement network pinned to the link; empty — the buyer chooses the network.
POST /v1/payment/link.title: Title on the payment page.

POST /v1/payment/link/info.document_url: Signed link to a PDF poster with the payment QR (for printing at the till). Empty if document generation is not enabled.
POST /v1/payment/link/info.url: Public URL of the payment page — give it to the buyer as a button, in an email or as a QR code.
POST /v1/payment/link/info.limit: Page size for the link's payments, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.

POST /v1/payment/qr.uuid: Invoice id in Oblodai. Either uuid or order_id is required; uuid takes priority.

POST /v1/payment/refund.address: Refund destination address. Defaults to the payment's payer_address; required only for Bitcoin/UTXO.
POST /v1/payment/refund.amount: Partial amount. Defaults to the full amount received.
POST /v1/payment/refund.order_id: Your order reference for the payment. Either uuid or order_id is required.
POST /v1/payment/refund.reference: Optional refund idempotency key: distinguishes two different refunds with the same (payment, address, amount); a repeat with the same value is deduplicated. This is not order_id.
POST /v1/payment/refund.uuid: Payment id. Either uuid or order_id is required.

POST /v1/payment/resend.uuid: Invoice id in Oblodai. Either uuid or order_id is required; uuid takes priority.

POST /v1/payment/resolve.action: accept — accept the partial payment, refund — return it to the payer.
POST /v1/payment/resolve.address: refund only: refund address. Defaults to the payment's recorded payer_address; if it is empty (Bitcoin/UTXO) the address is required, otherwise refund.no_address.
POST /v1/payment/resolve.network: refund only: refund network, defaults to the payment network.
POST /v1/payment/resolve.reference: refund only: your refund deduplication key.
POST /v1/payment/resolve.uuid: Payment UUID. Either uuid or order_id is required.

POST /v1/payment/send-email.email: Where to send it. Defaults to the payer_email set on the payment.
POST /v1/payment/send-email.uuid: Payment id in Oblodai. Either uuid or order_id is required.

POST /v1/payment/testing-webhook.status: Status in the body. Default paid.
POST /v1/payment/testing-webhook.url: Where to send the test body. If not provided, delivery goes to the project's registered endpoint; without an endpoint it fails with webhook.no_endpoint. Signed with the project endpoint's secret, including when url is passed explicitly.

POST /v1/payout.from_currency: Fund the payout by converting the balance. USDT → currency only.
POST /v1/payout.is_subtract: Who pays the network fee: true — amount+fee is debited from the balance and the recipient receives amount; false — the recipient receives amount-fee; not provided — the project fee-config.
POST /v1/payout.network: Network (tron, ethereum, …). Required for coins with several networks.
POST /v1/payout.url_callback: Custom webhook URL for this payout (passes the SSRF check). Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): delivery is signed with its secret.

POST /v1/payout/batch.on_error: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — halt processing after the first error.
POST /v1/payout/batch.payouts: Array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as POST /v1/payout; order_id is required on every item and serves as the idempotency key: a repeat returns the already created payout.
POST /v1/payout/batch.payouts.from_currency: Fund the payout by converting the balance. USDT → currency only.
POST /v1/payout/batch.payouts.is_subtract: Who pays the network fee: true — amount+fee is debited from the balance and the recipient receives amount; false — the recipient receives amount-fee; not provided — the project fee-config.
POST /v1/payout/batch.payouts.network: Network (tron, ethereum, …). Required for coins with several networks.
POST /v1/payout/batch.payouts.url_callback: Custom webhook URL for this payout (passes the SSRF check). Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): delivery is signed with its secret.

POST /v1/payout/cancel.uuid: Id of the payout (or refund) to cancel.

POST /v1/payout/fee-config/set.fee_on_recipient: true — the recipient pays the network fee (receives less); false — the merchant bears the fee.

POST /v1/payout/info.uuid: Invoice id in Oblodai. Either uuid or order_id is required; uuid takes priority.

POST /v1/payout/link.amount: Amount in currency, as a string; greater than zero.
POST /v1/payout/link.currency: Payout crypto asset (USDT, BTC, …); fiat is not possible.
POST /v1/payout/link.email: If set, the recipient receives an email with a "Claim funds" button; a delivery failure does not cancel link creation.
POST /v1/payout/link.expires_in_seconds: Link lifetime in seconds, clamped to 3600–2592000 (one hour to 30 days); without the field or with 0 the link lives 1 hour, not the maximum — set it explicitly.
POST /v1/payout/link.fee_bearer: Who pays the network fee: "recipient" (default — deducted from the amount, the recipient receives less) or "merchant" (the amount plus the fee is reserved, the recipient receives exactly amount).
POST /v1/payout/link.network: Payout network for the recipient (tron, bitcoin, …).
POST /v1/payout/link.note: Message to the recipient (shown on the claim page and in the email).
POST /v1/payout/link.passcode: Claim code — a second factor for the link: "auto" — we generate it and return it ONCE in the response, or your own (6–64 visible characters), empty — no code. Pass the code to the recipient over a channel SEPARATE from the link (it is not put into the email); after 10 incorrect attempts the link is locked.
POST /v1/payout/link.reference: Your deduplication key, unique per merchant; the Idempotency-Key header has no effect on this endpoint.
POST /v1/payout/link.title: Title — shown to the recipient on the claim page.

POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items: Up to 500 links per call; each one succeeds or fails independently, the response is aligned with the request indexes.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.amount: Amount in currency, as a string; greater than zero.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.currency: Payout crypto asset (USDT, BTC, …); fiat is not possible.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.email: If set, the recipient receives an email with a "Claim funds" button; a delivery failure does not cancel link creation.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.expires_in_seconds: Link lifetime in seconds, clamped to 3600–2592000 (one hour to 30 days); without the field or with 0 the link lives 1 hour, not the maximum — set it explicitly.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.fee_bearer: Who pays the network fee: "recipient" (default — deducted from the amount, the recipient receives less) or "merchant" (the amount plus the fee is reserved, the recipient receives exactly amount).
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.network: Payout network for the recipient (tron, bitcoin, …).
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.note: Message to the recipient (shown on the claim page and in the email).
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.passcode: Claim code — a second factor for the link: "auto" — we generate it and return it ONCE in the response, or your own (6–64 visible characters), empty — no code. Pass the code to the recipient over a channel SEPARATE from the link (it is not put into the email); after 10 incorrect attempts the link is locked.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.reference: Your deduplication key, unique per merchant; the Idempotency-Key header has no effect on this endpoint.
POST /v1/payout/link/batch.items.title: Title — shown to the recipient on the claim page.

POST /v1/payout/link/cancel.link_id: Payout link id (link_id from the creation response).

POST /v1/payout/link/cheque.claim_token: Claim secret from the payout link creation response. Stored only as a hash and never reissued — the cheque can be printed only while you still hold the token.
POST /v1/payout/link/cheque.lang: Document language — one of the 41 supported codes (en by default); the full list is in the document.unknown_lang error.

POST /v1/payout/link/info.link_id: Payout link id (link_id from the creation response).

POST /v1/payout/link/list.limit: How many links to return per page.
POST /v1/payout/link/list.offset: Offset from the start of the list (paging).

POST /v1/payout/mass.payouts: Array of up to 100 items; the fields of each are as in POST /v1/payout.
POST /v1/payout/mass.payouts.from_currency: Fund the payout by converting the balance. USDT → currency only.
POST /v1/payout/mass.payouts.is_subtract: Who pays the network fee: true — amount+fee is debited from the balance and the recipient receives amount; false — the recipient receives amount-fee; not provided — the project fee-config.
POST /v1/payout/mass.payouts.network: Network (tron, ethereum, …). Required for coins with several networks.
POST /v1/payout/mass.payouts.url_callback: Custom webhook URL for this payout (passes the SSRF check). Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): delivery is signed with its secret.
POST /v1/payout/mass.source: Origin label, applied to every item without its own source.

POST /v1/payout/refund-fee-config/set.fee_on_customer: true — the customer receives net (the customer pays the fee); false — the merchant pays the fee and the customer receives gross.

POST /v1/payout/validate.from_currency: Fund the payout by converting the balance. USDT → currency only.
POST /v1/payout/validate.is_subtract: Who pays the network fee: true — amount+fee is debited from the balance and the recipient receives amount; false — the recipient receives amount-fee; not provided — the project fee-config.
POST /v1/payout/validate.network: Network (tron, ethereum, …). Required for coins with several networks.
POST /v1/payout/validate.url_callback: Custom webhook URL for this payout (passes the SSRF check). Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): delivery is signed with its secret.

POST /v1/refund/batch.on_error: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — halt processing after the first error.
POST /v1/refund/batch.refunds: Array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as POST /v1/payment/refund; every item requires reference (idempotency key) and either uuid or order_id of the payment.
POST /v1/refund/batch.refunds.address: Refund destination address. Defaults to the payment's payer_address; required only for Bitcoin/UTXO.
POST /v1/refund/batch.refunds.amount: Partial amount. Defaults to the full amount received.
POST /v1/refund/batch.refunds.order_id: Your order reference for the payment. Either uuid or order_id is required.
POST /v1/refund/batch.refunds.reference: Optional refund idempotency key: distinguishes two different refunds with the same (payment, address, amount); a repeat with the same value is deduplicated. This is not order_id.
POST /v1/refund/batch.refunds.uuid: Payment id. Either uuid or order_id is required.

POST /v1/sandbox/deposit.amount: Amount in the invoice currency; empty — pay exactly what is due, anything else is a way to produce an under/overpayment.
POST /v1/sandbox/deposit.confirmations: How many confirmations the deposit arrived with; 0 — fully confirmed; fewer than required — a way to test the pending→confirmed transition (repeat the same txid with a higher number).
POST /v1/sandbox/deposit.invoice_id: UUID of the test invoice being "paid".
POST /v1/sandbox/deposit.txid: Repeating the same txid tests your idempotency; empty — a new txid.

POST /v1/sandbox/faucet.amount: Amount of test money, as a string; capped at 1000000 per call.
POST /v1/sandbox/faucet.idempotency_key: Safe-retry key; empty — every call creates a new top-up.

POST /v1/split/config/set.refund_hold_seconds: How many seconds to defer split settlement; range 0–7776000 (up to 90 days). 0 — send the shares immediately: you take on the risk that a refund becomes impossible.

POST /v1/split/recipient/optin.enabled: Allow other merchants to route split shares to your balance. true — enable receiving, false — disable (new rules targeting you stop being created; existing ones keep executing).

POST /v1/split/rule.address: External crypto address of the partner; the share leaves as a real on-chain transaction — irreversible. Exactly one recipient option: either address+network or merchant_id.
POST /v1/split/rule.merchant_id: Id of the partner merchant inside Oblodai; the share moves through internal accounting and is clawed back on a refund.
POST /v1/split/rule.network: Address network. Required together with address.
POST /v1/split/rule.note: Comment for yourself (shown in the rule list).
POST /v1/split/rule.percent: Share of every payment, as a string: "10" = 10 %, "2.5" = 2.5 %. Greater than 0 and at most 100, step 0.01 %; the sum of all rules cannot exceed 100 %.

POST /v1/test-webhook/payment.order_id: Your order_id, which is put into the test event body.
POST /v1/test-webhook/payment.status: Status in the body — from the status dictionary of this event type. Default paid (confirmed for a payout).
POST /v1/test-webhook/payment.url_callback: Where to send the test body.
POST /v1/test-webhook/payment.uuid: UUID of the object (payment, wallet or payout) put into the test event body.

POST /v1/test-webhook/payout.order_id: Your order_id, which is put into the test event body.
POST /v1/test-webhook/payout.status: Status in the body — from the status dictionary of this event type. Default paid (confirmed for a payout).
POST /v1/test-webhook/payout.url_callback: Where to send the test body.
POST /v1/test-webhook/payout.uuid: UUID of the object (payment, wallet or payout) put into the test event body.

POST /v1/test-webhook/wallet.order_id: Your order_id, which is put into the test event body.
POST /v1/test-webhook/wallet.status: Status in the body — from the status dictionary of this event type. Default paid (confirmed for a payout).
POST /v1/test-webhook/wallet.url_callback: Where to send the test body.
POST /v1/test-webhook/wallet.uuid: UUID of the object (payment, wallet or payout) put into the test event body.

POST /v1/transfer/batch.on_error: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — halt processing after the first error.
POST /v1/transfer/batch.transfers: Array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as POST /v1/transfer/to-user; every item requires order_id (idempotency key) and to_user_id (user UUID).
POST /v1/transfer/batch.transfers.order_id: Idempotency key: a repeat with the same order_id is a no-op; required in a transfer batch.
POST /v1/transfer/batch.transfers.to_user_id: Platform user id of the recipient (UUID, not username); a username is resolved to an id via the cabinet public profile /public/users/{username}.

POST /v1/transfer/to-personal.order_id: Idempotency key: a repeat with the same order_id is a no-op. Always send it, otherwise retrying the request after a network timeout creates a second transfer.

POST /v1/transfer/to-user.order_id: Idempotency key: a repeat with the same order_id is a no-op; required in a transfer batch.
POST /v1/transfer/to-user.to_user_id: Platform user id of the recipient (UUID, not username); a username is resolved to an id via the cabinet public profile /public/users/{username}.

POST /v1/wallet.currency: Symbol of the receiving currency (USDT, BTC, ETH, …).
POST /v1/wallet.order_id: Your customer/order identifier. Pins a dedicated permanent address to the customer.

POST /v1/wallet/block.is_force_block: true — block (the default when the field is omitted); false — unblock.

POST /v1/wallet/blocked-address-refund.memo: Destination tag/memo (XRP destination tag, XLM memo id, TON comment). Required for a classic address on a tag/memo network if the tag is not embedded in the X-/M-address.

POST /v1/wallet/qr.address: Arbitrary address to render into a QR code (PNG as a data: URI).

POST /v1/webhooks.url: HTTPS callback URL. SSRF check: private and local addresses are rejected.

POST /v1/payment/history.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payment/history.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).
POST /v1/payment/history.status: Filter by status (an exact value from the status vocabulary); empty returns all.
POST /v1/payment/history.kind: Ignored on this route (payout history only).

POST /v1/payout/history.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payout/history.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).
POST /v1/payout/history.status: Filter by status (an exact value from the status vocabulary); empty returns all.
POST /v1/payout/history.kind: payout — ordinary payouts, refund — refunds; empty returns both.

POST /v1/payment/services.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payment/services.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/payout/services.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payout/services.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/webhooks/deliveries.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/webhooks/deliveries.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/payment/link/list.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payment/link/list.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/split/rule/list.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/split/rule/list.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/payment/discount/list.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payment/discount/list.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/payment/accepted/list.limit: Page size, 1–100; out of range falls back to 25.
POST /v1/payment/accepted/list.offset: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

POST /v1/payout/calculate.amount: Payout amount as a decimal string.
POST /v1/payout/calculate.network: Payout network; required when the asset lives on several networks.
POST /v1/payout/calculate.is_subtract: true — the fee is debited from the balance on top of the amount (the recipient gets exactly amount); false — the fee is taken out of the payout.

POST /v1/payment/link/toggle.active: true — the link accepts payments; false — disabled (the page shows the link as inactive).

POST /v1/split/rule/delete.rule_id: Rule identifier from POST /v1/split/rule or the list.

POST /v1/payment/accepted/set.accepted: The full list of currency+network pairs payers may use; an empty list accepts everything in the catalog.

POST /v1/auto-withdraw/set.min_amount: Threshold: the sweep runs once the available balance of the asset reaches this amount; empty uses the network minimum.

POST /v1/auto-withdraw/delete.currency: Asset whose auto-withdrawal to switch off.

POST /v1/api-allowlist/add.cidr: IP or subnet in CIDR notation (203.0.113.7 or 203.0.113.0/24).

POST /v1/api-allowlist/remove.cidr: IP or subnet in CIDR notation (203.0.113.7 or 203.0.113.0/24).

POST /v1/api-allowlist/enable.enabled: true — accept API calls only from listed addresses; false — the list is kept but not enforced.

POST /v1/vrcs.enabled: true — enable auto-conversion of volatile deposits to USDT, false — disable; omit to read the current state.

POST /v1/merchants.email: Owner email; must be unique across merchants.
POST /v1/merchants.name: Display name of the merchant.

POST /v1/batch/info.failed: Failed with an error (with on_error stop, skipped items are counted here too).
POST /v1/batch/info.items: Page of items with the result or the error for each one.

POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.txid: Hash of the incoming transaction (once it is seen).
POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.url: Link to the hosted payment page.
POST /v1/link/{id}/checkout.url_return: "Back to shop" link shown before payment.

POST /v1/payment/cancel.destination_tag: XRP only: numeric destination tag the customer MUST include in the transfer (the "tag/memo of the recipient" field on an exchange or in a wallet). Empty on other networks.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.document_url: Signed link to the PDF cheque for this operation — opens without an API key, can be attached to an email or handed to the customer. Empty if document generation is not enabled.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.exchange_rate: Rate locked by this invoice (how much payment currency per 1 unit of the price currency) — payer_amount is calculated from it. Empty until the currency is chosen.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.expired_at: When the invoice expires (ISO 8601, like all time fields).
POST /v1/payment/cancel.is_final: true — the status is final and will not change again.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.is_multi: true — this is a currency-agnostic link, the customer has not chosen a currency/network yet.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.is_test: true — a sandbox invoice (dev shop): the money is not real, do not include it in live reconciliation.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.memo: XLM (Stellar) only: numeric memo (type ID) the customer MUST include in the transfer — the "memo" field on an exchange or in a wallet. Empty on other networks.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.merchant_amount: How much is (or will be) credited to you: amount_paid − commission. The network costs of collecting the deposit are borne by the gateway — they are NOT deducted from this amount.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.order_id: Your order number, passed at creation.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.paid_at: Moment of the actual payment — crediting of the last confirmed transfer (ISO 8601). null until the payment arrives. Distinguish it from updated_at, which shifts on any invoice change.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.payer_address: Address the first confirmed deposit came FROM — on account-based networks (EVM/Tron/Solana/TON); empty on UTXO. ⚠ This is NOT necessarily a refund address: the sender may be an exchange, the change of a UTXO transaction or the hot omnibus of a crypto on-ramp if the buyer paid by card. Check payer_address_is_refundable before refunding funds here.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.payer_address_is_refundable: true — payer_address belongs to the payer and address may be omitted in /v1/payment/refund (we refund to it). false — the refund address is unknown (UTXO/XRP, card payment via an on-ramp, address not recorded): ask the buyer for an address and pass address explicitly, otherwise the request is rejected with refund.no_address.

POST /v1/payment/cancel.payer_currency: Currency the customer pays in (for example, USDT). Empty for a currency-agnostic invoice (is_multi) until the customer picks a coin — it has no settlement currency yet.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.payer_email: Payer e-mail, if you passed one.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.rate_expires_at: When the rate will be refreshed (ISO 8601; the rate holds for ~5 min).
POST /v1/payment/cancel.required_confirmations: How many confirmations are needed for crediting (depends on the amount and the network).
POST /v1/payment/cancel.status: Status: select (the customer is choosing a currency) | created (waiting for payment) | confirm_check (payment seen, waiting for confirmations; with amount_remaining > 0 it is partial and the remainder is awaited) | paid | paid_over (overpayment) | wrong_amount (underpayment, deadline passed) | expired | cancelled.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.tx_list: All confirmed transfers that paid the invoice. Partial payment in several transfers is the regular wrong_amount scenario; the single txid at the top level is only the last one seen.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.tx_list.amount: Transfer amount in the payment currency.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.tx_list.height: Height of the block the transfer was confirmed in.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.tx_list.network: Network the transfer arrived on. On EVM it may differ from the invoice network: a deposit is credited on another chain with the same address too.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.txid: Hash of the incoming transaction (once it is seen).
POST /v1/payment/cancel.url: Link to the hosted payment page.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.url_return: "Back to shop" link shown before payment.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.url_success: Where to redirect after successful payment.
POST /v1/payment/cancel.uuid: Our payment id (use it in info/refund).

POST /v1/payment/refund.address: Address the funds were returned to.
POST /v1/payment/refund.amount: Refund amount in the payment coin.
POST /v1/payment/refund.is_final: true — the refund is in a terminal status.

POST /v1/payment/refund.payment_uuid: Id of the payment being refunded.

POST /v1/payout.amount: Payout amount in currency, debited from your balance.
POST /v1/payout.approval_required: true — the payout is awaiting approval (internal scenarios; always false for an API key).
POST /v1/payout.commission: Network fee withheld, in the payout currency. 0 — the gateway absorbed the fee.
POST /v1/payout.document_url: Signed link to the PDF cheque for this operation — opens without an API key, can be attached to an email or handed to the recipient. Empty if document generation is not enabled.
POST /v1/payout.fee_bearer: Who paid the network fee: gateway — the gateway absorbed it (commission = 0); merchant — the debited amount was increased by the fee and the recipient receives the requested amount in full (is_subtract=true, payout link with fee_bearer=merchant); recipient — the fee was withheld from the payout and the recipient receives less than requested.
POST /v1/payout.is_final: true — the status is final (paid / fail / cancel).
POST /v1/payout.is_refund: true — this is a payment refund, not a regular payout.
POST /v1/payout.memo: Destination tag/memo passed at creation (TON Jetton, exchange memo). Empty — no memo.
POST /v1/payout.order_id: Your payout number (reference). null for a refund: a refund has no identifier of yours, see payment_order_id.
POST /v1/payout.payer_amount: How much actually goes to the recipient's address: amount − commission.
POST /v1/payout.payment_order_id: Your order_id of the payment the refund was made for (null for a regular payout). A refund has no order_id of its own — it comes back null, and a refund must be reconciled with the order by this field.
POST /v1/payout.refund_for: Id of the payment being refunded (null if this is not a refund).
POST /v1/payout.source: api (via the integration) | manual (from the cabinet).
POST /v1/payout.status: Coarse status: check (created, waiting) | process (being sent/waiting for confirmations) | paid (confirmed — done) | awaiting_cosign (waiting for the second signature) | fail | cancel.
